passages.note: Concurrence vote on AB 1775, a consumption-lounge ancillary-business bill; Noes 5 of 68 cast is near-unanimous and does not speak to the ladder's legal-status question.

passages.provision_quote: (B) (i) Preparation or sale of noncannabis food or beverage products in compliance with all applicable provisions of the California Retail Food Code (Chapter 1 (commencing with Section 113700) of Part 7 of Division 104 of the Health and Safety Code) by a retailer or microbusiness licensed under this division in the area where the consumption of cannabis is allowed.
passages.note: Authorizes local jurisdictions to let already-licensed consumption lounges sell food and host live music, an ancillary-business axis the ladder does not order.

rows.reasoning: Both AB 1775 passages are Haney's own record (author attribution and a concurrence vote), but the bill's operative content only lets local jurisdictions permit food, beverage, and live-music sales at already-licensed cannabis consumption lounges; it assumes the existing licensed commercial market and does not match any rung's clause on cannabis's legal status, so no passage survives V2 to support a chair.
needs_source: Haney's own words or an on-question record on cannabis's basic legal status (e.g., a bill or statement setting or changing criminal penalties, medical-only limits, or the licensed/taxed commercial market itself), to evidence a rung on this ladder.
